text:
Predicates:
Taller(x, y) ::: x is taller than y.
CanBlock(x, y) ::: x can block y's shooting.
Jump(x) ::: x can jump when shooting.
GreatShooter(x) ::: x is a great shooter.
Michael :: a specific individual named Michael.
Windy :: a specific individual named Windy.
Peter :: a specific individual named Peter.
EveryoneTallerThan(x, y) ::: ∀z (Taller(z, y) → Taller(x, y))
Taller(x, y) ↔ ∃z (Taller(z, y) ∧ z ≠ x)
Michael is taller than everyone else ::: ∀x (x ≠ Michael → Taller(Michael, x))
Peter is taller than Michael ::: Taller(Peter, Michael)
Michael can block any shot from a person who does not jump ::: ∀x (¬Jump(x) → CanBlock(Michael, x))
Michael cannot block Windy’s shot ::: ¬CanBlock(Michael, Windy)
Every shooter who can jump when shooting is a great shooter ::: ∀x (Jump(x) → GreatShooter(x))
Question:
Peter can block Windy's shooting ::: CanBlock(Peter, Windy)

Premises:
Czech(miroslav) ∧ ChoralConductor(miroslav) ∧ Specialize(miroslav, renaissance) ∧ Specialize(miroslav, baroque)
∀x (ChoralConductor(x) → Musician(x))
∃x (Musician(x) ∧ Love(x, music))
Book(methodOfStudyingGregorianChant) ∧ Author(miroslav, methodOfStudyingGregorianChant) ∧ Publish(methodOfStudyingGregorianChant, year1946)
